1.7.formula: ( safe_divide ( sum ( [TOTAL_REVENUE] ) - sum ( [TOTAL_COGS] ) , sum ( [TOTAL_REVENUE] ) ) - safe_divide ( sum ( [PLAN_TOTAL_REVENUE] ) - sum ( [PLAN_TOTAL_COGS] ) , sum ( [PLAN_TOTAL_REVENUE] ) ) ) * 100
1.7.note: Ratio of totals: matches Excel only where one row = the reporting grain. The Excel aggregate equivalent is SUM(Table[..])/SUM(Table[..]). Review: when plan revenue is 0, the plan margin becomes 0 and the result silently becomes actual margin x 100. Excel's IFERROR blanks the whole row instead. If that matters, wrap it: if ( sum ( [PLAN_TOTAL_REVENUE] ) = 0 ) then null else ….

2.8.note: Valid only at single-month grain; across months it multiplies the period total by 12.

1.8.formula: if ( [GROSS_PROFIT] < 0 ) then 'Loss-making' else if ( safe_divide ( [GROSS_PROFIT] , [TOTAL_REVENUE] ) < 0.5 ) then 'Below Floor' else 'Healthy'
1.8.note: Row-level, like the Excel formula, so it is a true attribute you can group by. safe_divide gives 0 on zero revenue, so 'Below Floor', exactly as Excel's IFERROR(…,0). For per-account bucketing, wrap the sums in group_aggregate ( … , { [ACCOUNT] } , query_filters ( ) ). A bare sum() makes it a measure.

2.29.formula: if ( [HEALTH_SCORE] < 50 ) then 'At Risk' else if ( [HEALTH_SCORE] < 75 ) then 'Neutral' else 'Healthy'
2.29.note: Row-level, matching Excel. The original average() made it a measure; for an account-level band use group_aggregate ( average ( [HEALTH_SCORE] ) , { [ACCOUNT] } , query_filters ( ) ). A NULL score gives 'Healthy' in ThoughtSpot; Excel treats a blank as 0, giving 'At Risk'.

2.35.note: Row-level, matching Excel. The original mixed a row test with sum(), so its result depended on whether the tier was in the search. Case-insensitive on both sides.

2.45.note: Row-level, matching Excel. safe_divide gives 0 on a zero plan, so 'On Track', exactly as Excel's IFERROR(…,0). For a period-level status use the summed ratio, which makes it a measure.

2.30.note: Exact; NULL gives 'Standard' on both sides.

2.33.note: Tests against 1 instead of 0, so a NULL gives 'Churned' on both sides. With the original `= 0` test, NULL gives 'Active' in ThoughtSpot but 'Churned' in Excel (blank = 0). Confirm what NULL should mean.

2.32.note: Exact if the column is an integer; a DOUBLE column may render '12.0'.

2.34.formula: if ( contains ( [ACV_BAND] , '150K' ) or contains ( [ACV_BAND] , '500K+' ) ) then 'Enterprise' else 'Commercial'
2.34.note: Exact: ThoughtSpot contains and Excel SEARCH are both case-insensitive (probed 2026-10-06). Note that '150K' also matches e.g. '1150K'.

2.38.note: Row-level. Set the columns[] entry to MEASURE with aggregation: SUM to count EMEA rows. `=` is case-insensitive on both sides.

2.39.formula: if ( contains ( [BILLING_FREQUENCY] , 'month' ) ) then 'Monthly' else if ( contains ( [BILLING_FREQUENCY] , 'quarter' ) ) then 'Quarterly' else if ( contains ( [BILLING_FREQUENCY] , 'ann' ) or contains ( [BILLING_FREQUENCY] , 'year' ) ) then 'Annual' else 'Other'
2.39.note: Exact; both case-insensitive. Order matters: 'Semi-annual' gives 'Annual'.

2.40.note: Excel <> is case-insensitive, and ThoughtSpot != is likely the same (= is probed, != is not). A NULL currency gives 'USD' in ThoughtSpot and 'Non-USD' in Excel.

2.47.note: Nested two-argument concat: the formula reference documents two arguments only.

2.49.formula: if ( quarter_number ( [MONTH_END_DATE] ) = quarter_number ( today ( ) ) and year ( [MONTH_END_DATE] ) = year ( today ( ) ) ) then 1 else 0
2.49.note: Compares dates instead of building a label string, so it doesn't depend on the label format. Calendar quarter. quarter_number follows a fiscal calendar if the Model has one; Excel's ROUNDUP(MONTH/3) does not. Assumes the MONTH_END_DATE column used in 2.50.

2.50.note: Exact if the date is a true month end. A safer Excel equivalent is DAY(EOMONTH(d,0)).
